It takes months to do something like this and to bring it together. And so our thanks to everyone that had a hand involved in that, my personal thanks,
cues.zh: 也就是你们今天也听到的那些。我就不把所有名字再念一遍了，不过……或者说再数一遍，但要感谢 Teresa 做了这件事。最重要的是，我要感谢 Teresa Matlin 筹办了这次活动。真正联系我的是她，她也一直在组织这件事，还与学习中心的工作人员合作，确实把这件事办成了。办成这样的事、把大家聚到一起，需要好几个月。所以感谢所有参与其中的人，也献上我个人的感谢，

cues.zh: 第二个是讲讲执行功能，这个词如今正被

cues.zh: 还会讲自我调节

cues.zh: 以及这三个概念为什么彼此相关，还有为什么ADHD

cues.zh: 尤其是对它的管理

cues.en: to our clinical care of these individuals
cues.zh: 对我们为这些个体提供的临床照护而言

cues.en: by shifting to the
cues.zh: 通过转向

cues.zh: 执行功能和自我调节

cues.en: about ADHD,
cues.zh: 来看待ADHD，

cues.en: rather than continuing to view it as an attention disorder. As as Theresa and I have sometimes mentioned, ADHD suffers from a name that suggests it is insignificant.
cues.zh: 而不是继续把它看作一种注意力障碍。正如Theresa和我有时提到的，ADHD这个名字让人觉得它无关紧要。

cues.zh: 它没法与自闭症、双相障碍和精神分裂症相提并论。

cues.zh: 它没有那种社会关注度

cues.en: that all of those have. I mean, after all, it's just an attention disorder.
cues.zh: 而其他那些病都有。我的意思是，毕竟它只是个注意力障碍。

cues.zh: 而事实证明，ADHD 实际上——我会向你们展示——会干扰

cues.zh: 人类赖以生存的主要手段

cues.en: on this planet.
cues.zh: 在这个星球上。

cues.zh: 这使得它成为一种极其

cues.en: important disorder,
cues.zh: 重要的障碍，

cues.zh: 与我所提到的其他障碍同等重要，甚至更重要。而我今天的任务也是让你们相信这一点。

And you can see that I'm retired from the University of Massachusetts, but I'm not retired.

cues.zh: 我也不时代表制药行业发言，并作为顾问参与他们在 ADHD 市场的产品工作。这就是我的财务披露。我是个忙人。说到底，如果你想知道这种障碍，

cues.en: I will teach you. I will teach anyone, anywhere, anytime who asks,
cues.zh: 我会教你。我会教任何人，无论何时何地，只要他们开口问，

cues.en: who wants to know about ADHD.
cues.zh: 只要他们想了解 ADHD。

cues.en: And that is why I am here, thanks to
cues.zh: 这就是我来到这里的原因，感谢

cues.en: Theresa and her colleagues.
cues.zh: Theresa 和她的同事们。

cues.en: So let's begin first of all with just a very quick overview of what is ADHD,
cues.zh: 那么我们先从一个非常简短的概述开始：什么是 ADHD，

cues.en: because I can't teach you about why it might be a disorder of executive abilities,
cues.zh: 因为我没法讲清楚为什么它可能是一种执行功能障碍，

cues.en: unless we start at the beginning with what is it? How do we view it right now? And then how does this begin to fit into this new way of thinking about ADHD that I've been arguing about now for well over a decade or more? If you're not familiar with ADHD, is it a developmental disorder
cues.zh: 除非我们从最开头说起：它是什么？我们现在怎么看它？然后这又如何融入我十多年来一直主张的关于 ADHD 的这种新思考方式？如果你不熟悉 ADHD，它是一种发育障碍吗，

cues.en: of two psychological traits that are not emerging on time in the individual?
cues.zh: 由两种没有在个体身上按时显现的心理特质构成？

cues.en: That's important because ADHD is not a psychopathology.
cues.zh: 这很重要，因为 ADHD 不是一种精神病理。

cues.en: It is not a gross aberration in behavior like bipolar disorder,
cues.zh: 它不是像双相障碍那样行为上的严重异常，

cues.en: where you can recognize it at any age by a set of symptoms.
cues.zh: 后者在任何年龄都能通过一组症状识别出来。

cues.en: What separates ADHD from other individuals is a quantitative difference. There is a lag in the emergence of these very important
cues.zh: ADHD 与其他人的区别在于数量上的差异。这些非常重要的

cues.en: neuropsychological
cues.zh: 神经心理学

cues.en: traits.
cues.zh: 特质，其出现存在滞后。

cues.en: And so what distinguishes the disorder from other people is the degree of the lag, the quantitative difference,
cues.zh: 因此，这种障碍与他人的区别在于滞后的程度，即数量上的差异，

cues.en: not the qualitative difference. People with ADHD will hit the same milestones that other people meet for the most part. They will not hit them at the same time at the same rate. And when the parts of the brain that are responsible for these abilities
cues.zh: 而不是定性差异。ADHD 患者大多会达到其他人所达到的相同里程碑。但他们不会在同一时间、以相同速度达到。而当负责这些能力的大脑部位

cues.en: eventually reaches its maturity, which is in your early thirties,
cues.zh: 最终成熟时，也就是在你三十岁出头的时候，

cues.en: that is where they will level off
cues.zh: 他们就是在这里趋于平稳

cues.en: in their abilities.
cues.zh: 在能力方面。

cues.en: So that is not to say that they will outgrow the problem, some do, most do not. But it is to say that there is this developmental lag, a chronic
cues.zh: 所以这并不是说他们长大后就能摆脱这个问题——有些人会，大多数人不会。而是说存在这种发育滞后，一种长期

cues.en: delay
cues.zh: 延迟

cues.en: in the rate at which these traits are emerging within these individuals.
cues.zh: 体现在这些特质在这些人身上显现的速度上。

cues.en: Now, these problems fall into two domains, the domain of inattention after which the disorder is named and the domain of inhibition,
cues.zh: 现在，这些问题分为两个范畴：注意缺陷范畴——该障碍正是以此命名——以及抑制范畴，

cues.en: which gives rise to both the hyperactivity
cues.zh: 后者会导致多动

cues.en: and the impulsive
cues.zh: 和冲动

cues.en: behavior. We know that these arise early.
cues.zh: 行为。我们知道这些很早就出现了。

cues.en: On average, at least half or more people have their symptoms by age seven, many in the preschool years. A few of them were recognized in utero by mothers who said that this was an unusually
cues.zh: 平均而言，至少一半或更多人七岁前就出现症状，很多人是在学龄前。少数人在子宫内就被母亲察觉到，她们说这个胎儿异常地

cues.en: active little little fetus.
cues.zh: 活跃的小小胎儿。

cues.en: But on average, ninety eight percent by 16 years of age. That is to say that there was a small percentage of cases that do come on in adulthood, but it's very, very few. This is a childhood onset disorder for the most part.
cues.zh: 但平均而言，98%的人在16岁前出现症状。也就是说，有一小部分病例确实到成年才发病，但非常非常少。这基本上是一种儿童期起病的障碍。

cues.en: As you can see here, the disorder occurs across many places,
cues.zh: 如你所见，这种障碍会出现在许多地方，

cues.en: not just one, but it can fluctuate dramatically
cues.zh: 不只是一个地方，而且它会剧烈波动

cues.en: based upon the context.
cues.zh: 取决于具体情境。

cues.en: So people with ADHD are not equally severe in all domains on all tasks everywhere with all people. And that really causes a lot of consternation because if they can play video games for hours, but spend only five minutes on their homework, it makes it sound like it's a willful form of disobedience,
cues.zh: 所以，ADHD 患者并不是在所有领域、所有任务、所有场合、面对所有人时都同样严重。这确实让人非常不安，因为如果他能打几个小时的电子游戏，却只花五分钟做作业，听起来就像是故意不听话，

cues.en: as if this person has the ability, has the talent and is just choosing
cues.zh: 好像这个人有能力、有天赋，只是选择

cues.en: not to behave that way. But that distinction between video games and work, especially work for which there is no immediate consequence, tell someone like myself that there was a profound disturbance within the brain's executive system.
cues.zh: 不那样做。但电子游戏和工作之间的这种差别，尤其是那种不会带来即时后果的工作，会告诉我这样的人：大脑的执行系统存在严重紊乱。

cues.en: Because that is what explains the difference across these situations.
cues.zh: 因为正是这一点解释了这些情境之间的差异。

cues.en: Whereas if you didn't know that, you would start to blame the child
cues.zh: 而如果你不知道这一点，你就会开始责怪孩子

cues.en: for willfully disobeying you or just not caring or having some sort of a moral failure or just being lazy and so on. Many of the pejorative terms that have been used for these individuals. So it occurs across many places, but not everywhere.
cues.zh: 故意违抗你，或者根本不在乎，或者有某种道德缺陷，或者只是懒惰等等。人们用过许多贬义词来形容这些人。所以这种情况出现在很多地方，但并非所有地方都如此。

cues.en: And most importantly, to be a disorder, and this is what separates
cues.zh: 而最重要的是，要算作一种障碍，而这正是区分

cues.en: normal from abnormal,
cues.zh: 正常与异常、

cues.en: from non disordered disordered,
cues.zh: 非障碍与障碍的

cues.en: what separates them is there must be impairment in major life activities.
cues.zh: 关键所在：主要生活活动必须存在功能受损。

cues.en: It has to be interfering
cues.zh: 它必须干扰

cues.en: with
cues.zh: 到

cues.en: adaptive behavior,
cues.zh: 适应行为、

cues.en: self care,
cues.zh: 自我照料、

cues.en: family functioning, peer relationships,
cues.zh: 家庭功能、同伴关系、

cues.en: educational functioning. And then as we grow up, our relationships within the community, our ability to manage money, to drive,
cues.zh: 教育功能。然后随着我们长大，我们在社区中的关系、管理金钱的能力、开车、

cues.en: to, raise
cues.zh: 抚养

cues.en: our children, to enter into long term relationships with other people, our occupational functioning.
cues.zh: 子女、与他人建立长期关系，以及我们的职业功能。

cues.en: All of these are major life activities and ADHD needs to lead to impairment in one or more of these before it's a disorder. So having a high number of symptoms alone just makes you a sparkling personality.
cues.zh: 这些都是主要的生活活动，ADHD 必须导致其中一项或多项受损，才算是一种障碍。所以，仅仅症状数量多，只能说明你个性鲜明。

cues.en: What turns that into a disorder is that your sparklingness
cues.zh: 让这变成障碍的是，你的“闪耀”

cues.en: is a little too much so, and it is leading to impairment in areas where other people are not impaired.
cues.zh: 有点过头了，而且它正导致你在别人不受影响的方面出现功能受损。

cues.en: And that's the line when something becomes a disorder, the line of impairment.
cues.zh: 而某件事变成障碍的分界线，就是功能受损。

cues.en: And now, as you will see here, we also try to rule out other disorders because many other disorders produce deficits in attention.
cues.zh: 现在，正如你在这里会看到的，我们也会尝试排除其他障碍，因为许多其他障碍都会造成注意力缺陷。

cues.en: If someone comes into our clinic and says, I can't concentrate, we don't know what they have.
cues.zh: 如果有人来到我们的诊所，说“我无法集中注意力”，我们并不知道他们得了什么。

cues.en: Every disorder at one time or another, in one way or another, interferes with the six different circuits in the brain that gives rise to the six different kinds of attention that we possess.
cues.zh: 每一种障碍都会在某个时候、以某种方式，干扰大脑中六条不同的回路，而正是这些回路产生了我们所拥有的六种不同的注意力。

cues.en: So ADHD is not the only disorder of attention,
cues.zh: 所以 ADHD 并不是唯一的注意力障碍，

cues.en: but it is a relatively unique disorder in the kind of inattention
cues.zh: 但它在它所造成的那类注意力缺失上相对独特，

cues.en: that it produces.
cues.zh: 也就是它产生的那种。

cues.en: So let me explain.
cues.zh: 让我解释一下。

cues.en: First of all, ADHD starts out in early childhood as a problem in the area of inhibition.
cues.zh: 首先，ADHD 在童年早期表现为抑制功能方面的问题。

cues.en: The attention problems don't show up for two to four more years,
cues.zh: 注意力问题还要再过两到四年才会显现，

cues.en: but the problem with impulsiveness
cues.zh: 但冲动的问题

cues.en: starts out very early. This is where the hyperactivity and the restlessness are coming from. There was a problem with inhibiting the motor part of the brain,
cues.zh: 很早就开始了。多动和坐立不安正是由此而来。问题出在大脑对运动部分的抑制上，

cues.en: and therefore it is just on go
cues.zh: 因此它就一直处于启动状态

cues.en: all the time.
cues.zh: 一刻不停。

cues.en: That leads to the fidgeting,
cues.zh: 这会导致坐不住的小动作，

cues.en: the hyperactivity,
cues.zh: 多动，

cues.en: the restless, the squirming. It also leads to the verbal impulsiveness, the talkativeness, the interrupting others and so on. In addition to that, there was a cognitive impulsiveness.
cues.zh: 坐立不安、扭来扭去。它还会导致言语冲动、话多、打断别人等等。此外，还有认知冲动。

cues.en: They don't stop to think about things before they act.
cues.zh: 他们行动前不会停下来思考。

cues.en: They don't stop to consider what will happen later if I behave this way now. So there's a cognitive
cues.zh: 他们不会停下来考虑：如果我现在这样做，之后会发生什么。所以存在一种认知

cues.en: and a decision making impulsiveness
cues.zh: 和决策上的冲动性

cues.en: associated with the disorder. And that leads to a steep discounting
cues.zh: 与该障碍相关。这会导致对未来后果的急剧折现

cues.en: of future consequences.
cues.zh: 未来后果。

cues.en: What that means is that they don't value the future to the extent that other people of their age would do so. They live in the moment, the now that all that mattered, it's all that drives them, it's all that counts,
cues.zh: 这意味着，他们不像同龄人那样看重未来。他们活在当下，现在才是一切，是驱动他们的一切，也是唯一重要的，

cues.en: and what comes next is a far less value to them in their decision making. And so we look at them as individuals who basically are stuck in the now in terms of what matters to them, what is controlling them and how they're making their decisions.
cues.zh: 而接下来会发生什么，在他们的决策中价值要低得多。所以我们把他们看作基本上被困在“现在”里的人，就什么对他们重要、什么在控制他们、他们如何做决定而言。

cues.en: Now, they are also
cues.zh: 而且，他们也很

cues.en: very prone to distraction, but the distractibility is not a perceptual problem. It's not like the hear and see
cues.zh: 容易分心，但容易分心并不是感知问题。并不是说他们听到和看到

cues.en: distracting events more than others. The difference is they react to them when other people ignore them. It's a problem of inhibition.
cues.zh: 令人分心的事件比其他人多。区别在于，别人忽略这些事件时，他们会做出反应。这是抑制能力的问题。

cues.en: So that when they hear the noise or the sound or see the bird fly by the classroom window,
cues.zh: 所以，当他们听到噪声或声响，或看到鸟从教室窗外飞过时，

cues.en: The difference between them and us is they get up and talk about it. And the rest of us ignore it and go on with our work.
cues.zh: 他们和我们的区别在于，他们会起身谈论它。而我们其他人会忽略它，继续做自己的事。

cues.en: So there was a problem with distraction, but it is an inhibitory problem, not a perceptual problem. And then there was a set of symptoms that nobody talks about until the past couple of years,
cues.zh: 注意力分散确实有问题，但这是抑制控制的问题，不是知觉问题。还有一组症状，直到过去几年才有人谈论，

cues.en: but was always associated with ADHD back to the first paper on ADHD in a medical textbook in 1775
cues.zh: 但它一直与ADHD相关联，最早可追溯到1775年一本医学教科书里关于ADHD的首篇论文

cues.en: in Germany. Believe it or not, Melkior Weichert is the first person to describe this disorder. It's been around for well over two hundred years in the medical literature. This is not some Johnny come lately
cues.zh: 在德国。信不信由你，Melkior Weichert是第一个描述这种障碍的人。它在医学文献中已经存在了两百多年。这可不是什么新近才冒出来的

cues.en: disorder. And we have over 10,000
cues.zh: 障碍。而且我们有超过1万

cues.en: research papers
cues.zh: 篇研究论文

cues.en: on this disorder as well. But one of the things that we haven't spoken about since the 1960s,
cues.zh: 也是关于这种障碍的。但有一件事，从20世纪60年代以来我们就没再谈过，

cues.en: but now that we are coming back to, is that ADHD is just as much a disorder of emotion
cues.zh: 但现在我们又重新关注起来，那就是ADHD同样也是一种情绪障碍

cues.en: as it is of hyperactivity,
cues.zh: 就像多动症一样，

cues.en: inhibition, distraction and concentration.
cues.zh: 抑制、分心和专注力。

cues.en: People with ADHD are very impulsive in displaying their emotions, so that their emotions come up too quickly, too raw, too unmoderated.
cues.zh: ADHD 患者表达情绪时非常冲动，情绪来得太快、太原始、太不加节制。

cues.en: And as a result of that, they are often accused of being socially and emotionally immature.
cues.zh: 因此，他们常被说成在社交和情绪上不成熟。

cues.en: Now, this is not a mood disorder. Their moods are not irrational.
cues.zh: 这不是心境障碍。他们的情绪并非不理性。

cues.en: It's simply a disorder in which they can't regulate the emotions like other people can. The top down executive
cues.zh: 这只是一个障碍：他们无法像别人那样调节情绪。自上而下的执行

cues.en: control
cues.zh: 控制

cues.en: over normal emotion just isn't there to the degree that it should be. Now, the reason that we are so
cues.zh: 对正常情绪就是达不到应有的程度。我们之所以如此

cues.en: convinced that emotion needs to be put back into ADHD,
cues.zh: 确信情绪必须重新纳入 ADHD，

cues.en: is because this set of symptoms accounts for many of the impairments
cues.zh: 是因为这组症状解释了许多功能损害，

cues.en: that can't be explained by the more traditional
cues.zh: 而这些损害无法用更传统的

cues.en: symptoms of the disorder. Not the least of which is it's the single best predictor of why you have no friends.
cues.zh: 这种障碍的症状。尤其是，它是预测你为什么没朋友的最佳单项指标。

cues.en: Other people can forgive you, your restless behavior, your fidgeting, your distractibility,
cues.zh: 别人可以原谅你，原谅你不安的行为、坐立不安、容易分心，

cues.en: your physity, your fizziness, you're you're disrupting them. But what they don't forgive is anger and frustration and hostility and reactive aggression,
cues.zh: 你的身体动作、你的烦躁不安，你在打扰他们。但他们不会原谅的是愤怒、挫败感、敌意和反应性攻击，

cues.en: so that when things provoke you and upset you,
cues.zh: 所以当事情刺激你、让你心烦时，

cues.en: if you have ADHD, your emotions are up and out and the damage is done before you've had a chance to get any traction
cues.zh: 如果你有ADHD，你的情绪会立刻爆发出来，还没来得及控制住，伤害就已经造成了

cues.en: over moderating this and bringing your emotions to be more consistent with the situation and with your long term welfare.
cues.zh: 去调节情绪，让它更符合当前情境和你的长期利益。

cues.en: So we are now realizing, and many papers have been written this year making this case, that ADHD is just as much a problem with impulsive emotion
cues.zh: 所以我们现在意识到，今年也有很多论文论证了这一点：ADHD在情绪冲动方面的问题

cues.en: as it is with impulsive behavior, impulsive cognition, and impulsive speech.
cues.zh: 和它在行为冲动、认知冲动、言语冲动方面的问题一样严重。

cues.en: And it explains a lot about these individuals, not the least of which is of course their social difficulties.
cues.zh: 这也解释了这些人的很多表现，当然尤其是他们的社交困难。

cues.en: But it's also one of the best predictors of their driving problems, their financial problems, their marital problems, their child rearing problems. And it's one of the main reasons why they will be fired from a job four times more often than other people are likely to do. You don't get fired because you're distractible,
cues.zh: 但它也是预测他们驾驶问题、财务问题、婚姻问题、育儿问题的最有力指标之一。它也是他们被解雇的频率达到其他人四倍的主要原因之一。你不会因为容易分心而被解雇，

cues.en: but you will get fired if you are angry with the customers and if you will blow up and are impatient and are easily frustrated.
cues.zh: 但如果你对客户发火，动不动就爆发、没耐心、容易烦躁，你就会被解雇。

cues.en: So this is a domain of ADHD that is underappreciated,
cues.zh: 所以这是ADHD中一个被低估的领域，

cues.en: but is now being put back into our models and theories and explanations
cues.zh: 但现在正被重新纳入我们的模型、理论以及

cues.en: of the disorder. Now, one final caveat before moving on. The hyperactivity declines so steeply with age that by late adolescence,
cues.zh: 对这种障碍的解释中。现在，继续之前最后提醒一点。多动症状随年龄下降得如此急剧，以至于到青春期后期，

cues.en: and certainly by adulthood, it is of no diagnostic value whatsoever.
cues.zh: 而到了成年期，它绝对不再有任何诊断价值。

cues.en: Adults with ADHD are not hyperactive.
cues.zh: 患ADHD的成年人并不表现出多动。

cues.en: They feel internally like they are. They feel a need to be busy and restless and doing multiple projects. They often say that they're good at multitasking.
cues.zh: 他们内心觉得自己仍然多动。他们觉得自己需要忙碌、坐立不安，同时做多个项目。他们常说自己擅长多任务处理。

cues.en: Well, you are if you finish the things you start, but they don't finish anything.
cues.zh: 嗯，你要是能把自己开始的事做完，那才算；可他们什么都做不完。

cues.en: And so this is not multitasking.
cues.zh: 所以这可不是多任务处理。

cues.en: You know, this is distractibility.
cues.zh: 你知道，这是容易分心。

cues.en: But they are not climbing on furniture, sliding down banisters and doing all of the other gross motor hyperactivity
cues.zh: 但他们不会爬上家具、顺着栏杆往下滑，也不会做出其他各种粗大运动性的多动表现

cues.en: that we see in the young children. So please pay attention to that, adults with ADHD are not hyperactive.
cues.zh: 这些是我们在幼儿身上看到的。所以请注意，患 ADHD 的成年人并不表现为多动。

cues.en: Now, the inattention domain is much, much more than inattention.
cues.zh: 而注意力不集中这个维度，远不只是注意力不集中。

cues.en: But let's start with the inattentiveness.
cues.zh: 但我们先从注意力不集中说起。

cues.en: First of all, you need to understand that there are six different kinds of attention in your brain and ADHD does not cut a wide swath through all of them.
cues.zh: 首先，你要明白，大脑里有六种不同的注意力，而ADHD并不会把它们全都广泛影响一遍。

cues.en: It is particularly
cues.zh: 它尤其

cues.en: salient in one area
cues.zh: 在一个领域里很突出

cues.en: that other disorders are much less likely to have their impact on. And that is persistence
cues.zh: 其他障碍远不太可能对这个领域产生影响。那就是坚持

cues.en: toward the future.
cues.zh: 面向未来。

cues.en: There was a very special kind of attention,
cues.zh: 有一种非常特殊的注意力，

cues.en: you call it sustained attention,
cues.zh: 你称之为持续注意，

cues.en: but it is persistence
cues.zh: 但它其实是坚持

cues.en: toward the future, toward goals, toward tasks, toward what is coming up or what I need to be doing. It is attention to the later in your life,
cues.zh: 面向未来、面向目标、面向任务、面向即将发生的事或我该做的事。它关注的是你人生中更靠后的部分，

cues.en: not the now. People with ADHD
cues.zh: 而不是当下。ADHD患者

cues.en: attend to the now just fine.
cues.zh: 对当下的注意完全没问题。

cues.en: But as you get older,
cues.zh: 但随着年龄增长，

cues.en: you spend more and more of your time looking ahead and preparing for what is coming next and setting your own goals or following up on the tasks and goals and assignments given to you by other important people in your life.
cues.zh: 你会花越来越多时间向前看，为接下来要发生的事做准备，设定自己的目标，或者跟进生活中其他重要的人交给你的任务、目标和安排。

cues.en: And so what ADHD disrupts is persistence over time toward that future. It is the only future directed form of inattention
cues.zh: 所以ADHD破坏的是：朝着那个未来持续坚持的能力。它是唯一一种面向未来的注意力缺失

cues.en: that we see. And that is how we can diagnose it from schizophrenia and anxiety disorders and panic attacks and depression,
cues.zh: 形式，这是我们观察到的。也正因如此，我们能把它与精神分裂症、焦虑障碍、惊恐发作和抑郁症区分开来，

cues.en: all of which interfere with attention, but not in this way.
cues.zh: 这些都会干扰注意力，但不是以这种方式。

cues.en: So this is a problem with sustaining action over time towards your goals and the future more generally.
cues.zh: 所以，这关系到能否长期坚持朝着目标、以及更广义地朝着未来行动。

cues.en: Now, the ability to persist is coupled with the ability to resist
cues.zh: 而坚持的能力，与抵抗

cues.en: reacting to irrelevant events. I've already spoken about that. It's an inhibitory problem. That's the source of the distractibility.
cues.zh: 对无关事件作出反应的能力相耦合。我前面已经讲过。这是个抑制性问题。这就是易分心的根源。

cues.en: So that they are very prone to being easily distracted by irrelevant events that have nothing to do with the goal, the task or the future at hand. And this is what captures their behavior and leads them off task and gets them skipping from one uncompleted activity to another,
cues.zh: 所以他们很容易被无关事件分心，这些事件与手头的目标、任务或未来毫无关系。而这会支配他们的行为，让他们偏离任务，从一项未完成的活动跳到另一项，

cues.en: is this problem with impulsive
cues.zh: 就是这种冲动

cues.en: responding to irrelevant events.
cues.zh: 对无关事件作出反应的问题。

cues.en: Now, there is an interesting problem coupled with that, and it has nothing to do with attention. All of us occasionally get distracted by things we didn't plan on. And we have to stop what we're doing and attend to those things. There are important interruptions that take place in your day.
cues.zh: 现在，与此相关还有一个有趣的问题，而且它跟注意力无关。我们所有人偶尔都会被计划外的事情分心。这时我们必须停下正在做的事，去处理那些事情。一天当中总会出现一些重要的干扰。

cues.en: But what you do is once you've dealt with the interruption, you return to the task at hand, the incompleted goal, the future that lies before you recaptures your behavior.
cues.zh: 但你接下来要做的是：一旦处理完这个干扰，就回到手头的任务上，那个尚未完成的目标，那个摆在眼前的未来会重新抓住你的行为。

cues.en: That doesn't happen with people with ADHD.
cues.zh: ADHD 人群不会这样。

cues.en: Once distracted,
cues.zh: 一旦分心，

cues.en: they do not reengage the incompleted goal, they are off on a tangent from one to another to another.
cues.zh: 他们不会重新回到未完成的目标，而是不断跑题，从一个话题岔到另一个，再岔到另一个。

cues.en: So that that is where the now, so to speak, is pulling them along by the nose
cues.zh: 所以可以说，正是“当下”在牵着他们的鼻子走。

cues.en: when you and I get back to the work we had planned to do, the goals, the assignments, the instructions and so on. Now, this problem with task re engagement has nothing to do with attention.
cues.zh: 当你我重新回到原本计划要做的工作、目标、任务、指令等等时，要知道，这种重新投入任务的问题与注意力无关。

cues.en: It is the most important feature of what is called working memory.
cues.zh: 它是所谓工作记忆最重要的特征。

cues.en: Working memory is one of the big seven executive functions.
cues.zh: 工作记忆是七大执行功能之一。

cues.en: Working memory is consciously holding in mind,
cues.zh: 工作记忆是有意识地在脑中保持，

cues.en: what your goal is, how you plan to get there and what progress you are making toward that goal.
cues.zh: 你的目标是什么、你打算如何达成，以及你正朝着目标取得什么进展。

cues.en: Memory put to work or as I explain it to patients, remembering
cues.zh: 把记忆投入工作，或者按我向患者解释的说法，就是记住

cues.en: to do.
cues.zh: 要做的事。

cues.en: This is not memory. This is not storage and retrieval of facts and knowledge.
cues.zh: 这不是记忆。这不是对事实和知识的存储与提取。

cues.en: This is remembering what you're doing. What was the goal? What was the plan?
cues.zh: 这是在记住你正在做什么。目标是什么？计划是什么？

cues.en: How far along that road am I to accomplishing that goal? And that governs your behavior.
cues.zh: 我在这条路上距离实现那个目标还有多远？而它支配着你的行为。

cues.en: That's what takes over from the now, is what you should be doing. It's what you start to lose in your fifties. At my age, I'm 63 or will be shortly. It's what women lose even more when they hit perimenopause.
cues.zh: 这种记忆接管了当下，告诉你应该做什么。这就是你五十多岁时开始失去的东西。到我这个年纪，我63岁，或者快63了。女性在进入围绝经期后失去得更多。

cues.en: So what you are losing is your working memory.
cues.zh: 所以你失去的是工作记忆。

cues.en: You don't forget information,
cues.zh: 你不会忘掉信息，

cues.en: you forget what you were doing.
cues.zh: 你忘的是自己正在做什么。

cues.en: You walk into a room, something distracts you and now you can't remember why you entered the room.
cues.zh: 你走进一个房间，有东西让你分心，然后就想不起自己为什么进来了。

cues.en: So having ADHD is like aging times a 100
cues.zh: 所以患ADHD就像衰老速度快了一百倍

cues.en: or being little menopausal women, however you want to think about it. But
cues.zh: 或者像个小更年期妇女，随你怎么理解。但

cues.en: so what they are impaired in is memory put to work,
cues.zh: 所以他们受损的是把记忆投入使用，

cues.en: remembering
cues.zh: 记住

cues.en: to do.
cues.zh: 要做的事。

cues.en: So if they are forgetful during the day, it's not knowledge they're forgetting,
cues.zh: 所以如果他们白天健忘，忘掉的不是知识，

cues.en: it's what they're supposed to be doing, where they're supposed to be going, what calls to them by way of their goals and their tasks and so on. So that's your disorder, but you can see that it's much more than a disorder of attention. The fact that working memory is involved in this and that inhibition is involved in this, those are two of the seven big executive functions given to you by this massive frontal lobe in your brain. And that opens the door to the possibility that ADHD
cues.zh: 而是自己该做什么、该去哪里，自己的目标、任务等等在提醒自己做什么。所以这就是这种障碍，但你能看出，它远不只是注意力障碍。工作记忆参与其中，抑制也参与其中，这两者都是你大脑里这块巨大额叶赋予你的七大执行功能中的两个。而这打开了一种可能性：ADHD

cues.en: is EFDD.
cues.zh: 就是 EFDD。

cues.en: And the question then is, are the other five also impaired?
cues.zh: 那么问题就来了：另外五种执行功能是否也受损？

cues.en: Is this a very focal disorder of executive ability, hitting only working memory or working memory and inhibition as some people have argued? Or does it hit all of them? Is it a pervasive disorder?
cues.zh: 这是一种非常局灶性的执行能力障碍，只影响工作记忆，还是像一些人主张的那样只影响工作记忆和抑制？还是说它会影响到所有执行功能？它是一种广泛性障碍吗？

cues.en: Now to answer that question, we're gonna have to take a detour into executive functioning. And we're gonna have to talk about what that happens to be. Now, before I do that, I did wanna give you a slide in your handout that does talk about the prevalence of the disorder, how common it is and so forth. But my time is so precious today that I don't wish to waste it with well known facts and figures that are out there and easily available to you. But just in passing, you should know this is a very prevalent disorder. That it's about seven point five percent of children and nearly five point five percent of adults have this disorder. It is universal, it is worldwide, it is seen in all countries ever studied. It's not just a US disorder,
cues.zh: 现在要回答这个问题，我们得先绕道讲一下执行功能，还得说明它到底是什么。在此之前，我本来想给大家看讲义里的一页幻灯片，讲这种障碍的患病率、有多常见等等。但今天时间太宝贵，我不想把时间浪费在众所周知、你们也很容易查到的数据和事实上。不过顺带说一下，你们应该知道这是一种非常常见的障碍：大约 7.5% 的儿童和近 5.5% 的成年人患有这种障碍。它是普遍存在的，是世界性的，在所有研究过的国家都能见到。它不只是美国的障碍，

cues.en: as some critics have argued,
cues.zh: 正如一些批评者所主张的，

cues.en: but it is not evenly spread across the populations.
cues.zh: 但它在各人群中的分布并不均匀。

cues.en: Three times more common in boys than girls, but that sex difference disappears by adulthood when it is equally common in men and women. We don't know why the gender difference dissipates,
cues.zh: 男孩中的发生率是女孩的三倍，但到成年后这种性别差异会消失，届时男女的发生率相同。我们不知道这种性别差异为何会消退，

cues.en: but it does. We also know that it's more common in lower middle class families. It's more common in population dense than rural areas.
cues.zh: 但它确实会消退。我们还知道，它在中下阶层家庭中更常见。它在人口稠密地区比在农村地区更常见。

cues.en: It's also more common in children in the military
cues.zh: 这种情况在军人家庭的孩子中也更常见

cues.en: and the children of other professions like the performing arts and music and door to door sales and athletes.
cues.zh: 以及其他职业家庭的孩子，比如表演艺术、音乐、上门推销和运动员家庭。

cues.en: The reason for all of those differences
cues.zh: 所有这些差异的原因

cues.en: is this is where adults with ADHD tend to go as they grow up.
cues.zh: 是因为患 ADHD 的成年人长大后往往会进入这些领域。

cues.en: And because ADHD is the most genetically influenced psychiatric disorder we know of,
cues.zh: 而且，ADHD 是我们已知受遗传影响最大的精神障碍，

cues.en: rivaled only by autism and bipolar disorder and far more prevalent than either of those disorders.
cues.zh: 只有自闭症和双相障碍能与之相比，而且它比这两种障碍都常见得多。

cues.en: If you have ADHD and you're an adult and you start self selecting into certain careers because that's where you tend to function a little better,
cues.zh: 如果你是患有ADHD的成年人，开始主动选择进入某些职业，因为在这些领域你往往能表现得更好一些，

cues.en: like the military, well guess what, more of your children are going to have the same disorder that you had by virtue of the genetics alone. So there's nothing unique to athletics or the military.
cues.zh: 比如军队，那你猜怎么着，你会有更多孩子仅凭遗传就患上和你一样的障碍。所以体育或军队并没有什么特别之处。

cues.en: It has to do with where people with ADHD are likely to find themselves
cues.zh: 这与ADHD患者可能最终进入哪些领域有关，

cues.en: functioning with less impairment
cues.zh: 在那里他们发挥功能时受损更少，

cues.en: than they would had they chosen some other occupation,
cues.zh: 相比他们选择其他职业时，

cues.en: like law or science or medicine or technology. Doesn't mean they can't go into those professions,
cues.zh: 比如法律、科学、医学或技术。这并不意味着他们不能进入这些职业，

cues.en: just means that they are far less likely to be in them than our other people in the general population.
cues.zh: 只是意味着，与普通人群中的其他人相比，他们从事这些职业的可能性要小得多。

cues.en: Now, back to the question I was raising, is ADHD EFDD?
cues.zh: 现在，回到我提出的问题：ADHD 就是 EFDD 吗？

cues.zh: 要回答这个问题，我们得谈谈执行功能，

cues.en: what it is.

cues.en: But I can assure you that ADHD
cues.zh: 但我可以保证，ADHD

cues.zh: 一定是 EFDD。

cues.en: We could stop the lecture right here.

cues.en: The neuroanatomy
cues.zh: 从神经解剖上看，

cues.en: of ADHD
cues.zh: ADHD

cues.en: is the neuroanatomy
cues.zh: 就是

cues.en: of the executive brain.
cues.zh: 执行脑的神经解剖。

cues.en: The executive brain as Carl Preibram first coined the term is what the frontal lobes do.
cues.zh: 执行脑这个概念，最早由 Carl Preibram 提出，指的就是额叶的功能。

cues.en: And although he didn't go on to particularly define what he meant by executive functioning, he gets credit as the first person to coin the term.
cues.zh: 尽管他后来并没有具体定义自己所说的执行功能，但他仍被认为是第一个提出这个词的人。

cues.en: But what he was trying to do is describe why primates and especially humans have this massive frontal lobe to their brain.
cues.zh: 但他想做的，是解释为什么灵长类动物、尤其是人类，大脑会有如此巨大的额叶。

cues.en: And the history of that goes back another hundred years or more to the middle eighteen hundreds, efforts to study what do parts of the brain do, what does the frontal lobe do. The term executive functioning just sneaks in as one possible description
cues.zh: 而这段历史还要再往前推一百多年，到19世纪中叶，人们努力研究大脑各部位分别做什么、额叶做什么。“执行功能”这个术语就这样悄然出现，作为一种可能的描述

cues.en: for these activities
cues.zh: 用来描述这些活动

cues.en: of this executive brain.
cues.zh: 也就是这个“执行脑”的活动。

cues.en: We know that there are at least five structures involved in the executive brain. We know that they form three executive networks and we know that ADHD interferes with all three to varying degrees. So clinicians
cues.zh: 我们知道，执行脑至少涉及五种结构。我们知道它们构成三个执行网络，而ADHD会不同程度地干扰这三个网络。所以，临床医生

cues.en: and parents, one of the reasons you see such heterogeneity
cues.zh: 和家长，你们之所以会看到ADHD如此大的异质性，

cues.en: in ADHD is it depends on which of these circuits has been hit the most.
cues.zh: 原因之一就在于：这取决于哪个回路受影响最严重。

cues.en: They're all affected, but not all to the same degree in each person who possesses the disorder.
cues.zh: 它们全都受到影响，但在每个患此障碍的人身上，受影响的程度并不相同。

cues.zh: 在这里，外侧表面，从大脑中心往回延伸到那个结构。这被称为“什么”网络，因为你头脑中保持的内容、工作记忆将引导你的行为，也就是你的运动系统。

cues.zh: 这样大脑中的其他信号就不会发出、不会让你分心。然后它会用你的想法、你的心理表征

cues.zh: 来引导那个运动行为

cues.zh: 第二个要继续讲的网络

cues.en: is the WEN network, the timing network. This one surprises people because it's not often talked about in relationship to ADHD, unless you read some of my books or you happen to be familiar with the frontal lobes.
cues.zh: 是WEN网络，也就是计时网络。这个网络会让人惊讶，因为谈到ADHD时很少提到它，除非你读过我的一些书，或者碰巧熟悉额叶。

cues.en: This is the WEN network, it goes from the same outside surface of the frontal lobe back through that basal ganglia and now to the cerebellum.
cues.zh: 这就是WEN网络，它从额叶同样的外表面出发，向后穿过基底神经节，再到达小脑。

cues.en: The old ancient brain at the back part of the brain. We often think of the cerebellum as important for the grace and the movement and the timeliness of our actions like in gymnastics or dance, or just the general fluidity
cues.zh: 大脑后部的古老脑区。我们常认为小脑对动作的优雅、运动与时机很重要，比如体操或舞蹈，或者只是整体的流畅性

cues.en: of our behavior.
cues.zh: ——就我们的行为而言。

cues.en: But the cerebellum is also just as important for the grace and the timing of our thoughts,
cues.zh: 但小脑对我们思维的优雅与时机也同样重要，

cues.en: not just our actions.
cues.zh: 不只是动作。

cues.en: It's as much involved in higher cognitive activity
cues.zh: 它同样参与高级认知活动

cues.en: as is the frontal lobe. Indeed, an injury to the cerebellum can sometimes mimic a frontal lobe injury, causing neurologists difficulty in finding out where is the problem.
cues.zh: 和额叶一样。事实上，小脑损伤有时会模仿额叶损伤，让神经科医生难以找出问题所在。

cues.en: This is the timing circuit of the brain. We call it the when network.
cues.zh: 这是大脑的计时回路。我们称之为“when网络”。

cues.en: And it explains why ADHD
cues.zh: 这解释了为什么ADHD

cues.en: is the worst disorder when it comes to time management. There is no disorder as bad as this one, four to five times worse than any other disorder we have seen in terms of its interference with the timing and the timeliness of one's actions.
cues.zh: 在时间管理方面是最严重的障碍。没有比这更糟糕的障碍了，在干扰一个人行动的时间感和及时性方面，它比其他任何障碍都要严重四到五倍。

cues.en: Indeed, it eviscerates
cues.zh: 事实上，它掏空了

cues.en: your sense of time itself,
cues.zh: 你对时间本身的感知，

cues.en: which is why people with the disorder are adrift
cues.zh: 这就是为什么患有这种障碍的人会迷失

cues.en: in time and can't deal as well as others with this invisible dimension of our lives that becomes increasingly important
cues.zh: 在时间中，无法像其他人那样应对我们生活中这个无形的维度，而这个维度正变得越来越重要

cues.en: as we grow older. Three year olds don't have to be timely, 30 year olds do or they get fired.
cues.zh: 随着我们年龄的增长。三岁的孩子不必守时，三十岁的人必须守时，否则就会被解雇。

cues.en: So of all of the deficits, this will be the most devastating
cues.zh: 在所有缺陷中，这个最具破坏性

cues.en: and it is also the most impaired.
cues.zh: 而且受损也最严重。

cues.zh: 现在，大脑的第三条回路

cues.zh: 是热回路，

cues.zh: 也就是 Y 回路。同样，我们从额叶

cues.zh: 到额叶中线

cues.zh: 再到这里的杏仁核。

cues.zh: 这是情绪调节回路。

cues.zh: 所以它才叫热回路。

cues.zh: 就来自这里。

cues.zh: 执行控制中枢

cues.zh: 所以，冲动情绪就是从这儿来的——不耐烦、挫败感、容易发怒、容易激动、容易兴奋，

cues.en: the overreacting to events and indeed in a subset of people, the reactive aggression.
cues.zh: 对事情反应过度，而在部分人身上，就是反应性攻击。

cues.zh: ADHD 患者并不是掠夺成性，也不是精神病态。

cues.zh: 且极具破坏性，

cues.zh: 关于这些在我们生活中无处不在的测验。每天，美国有成千上万的人
